summary: Added eight multilingual sources in Polish, French, Portuguese, Chinese, Spanish and German. The Polish poll contributes only to philosophers; other reuse is individually scoped.
next: Expand independent blogs, reader communities and non-Western philosophical criticism; begin the separate literary-fiction corpus.

sources.title: Filozofowie ważni i bliscy — wyniki plebiscytu
sources.note: Among 135 respondents, the importance ranking begins Plato, Aristotle, Kant; personal closeness begins Socrates and Nietzsche and includes Tischner and Kolakowski. Votes used a 3–2–1 scheme.

targets.P: Direct Polish reader evidence distinguishing perceived importance from personal resonance.

sources.limits: Self-selected small readership; importance and closeness are separate source rankings. Follow-up breakdown is the same poll, not another source.

sources.title: Paweł Okołowski: Lukrecjusz ze Lwowa
sources.author: Paweł Okołowski; interviewed by Filip Kobiela
sources.note: Okolowski argues Lem's essays form a philosophical system obscured by his fiction's fame and difficult discursive prose. He contrasts Summa and Dialogues with fictional narratives.

targets.A: Adds technology and philosophical nonfiction alongside a fiction-versus-essay distinction.
targets.N: Identifies Summa and Dialogues as discursive works requiring separate reception evidence.
targets.B: Makes an explicit case for Lem's philosophical books.
targets.P: Provides a contested expert argument for Lem's philosopher eligibility.

sources.limits: A sympathetic specialist's interpretation; outdated English-publication comments are not treated as current availability.

sources.title: La carrière française de John Rawls
sources.author: Ophélie Desmons
sources.note: Reviewing Hauchecorne, Desmons explains Rawls's delayed French canonization and conflicting political readings. International circulation changes a book's interpreted meaning through local institutions and mediators.

targets.A: Adds empirical canon/reception history for a major political book.
targets.N: Supports political-intellectual-history nonfiction and reception context.
targets.B: Warns against treating one country's reading of Theory of Justice as universal.
targets.P: Separates Rawls's philosophical work from its shifting public labels.

sources.limits: French reception case study, not direct validation of Rawls's arguments; English translation of the reviewed monograph unresolved.

sources.title: Un nouveau Spinoza : entretien avec Bernard Pautrat
sources.author: Marc Lebiez; Bernard Pautrat
sources.note: Pautrat explains revised texts, consistent translation of Latin terms and a reading of Ethics' geometric order as substantive argument. He describes transformative reading, not merely admiration.
candidates: Treatise on the Emendation of the Intellect

targets.A: Adds translation and textual-transmission evidence for philosophical classics.
targets.N: Shows why edition quality matters for argumentative nonfiction.
targets.B: Supports an edition-sensitive account of Ethics' method.
targets.P: Adds French scholarly reception of Spinoza beyond summary reference.

sources.location: Interview on edition rationale, translation consistency and geometric order
sources.limits: French edition and editor's own interpretation; not an English-edition recommendation.

sources.title: Resenha: Sair da Grande Noite — Achille Mbembe
sources.note: The review presents decolonization as opening possible futures rather than merely auditing independence. It connects Mbembe to Fanon and Jean-Marc Ela and examines hybrid theoretical-autobiographical writing.

targets.A: Adds Brazilian reception of Cameroonian political thought.
targets.N: Supports decolonization nonfiction and its narrative form.
targets.B: Adds philosophical arguments about postcolonial futures and knowledge.
targets.P: Documents Mbembe's intellectual dialogue with Fanon and Ela.

sources.limits: Portuguese translation reviewed; the source is one article, not each cited book or DOI version.

sources.title: 学习哲学，要读读哪些书呢？
sources.note: The departmental list organizes Chinese and Western philosophy by study area, including Zhu Xi, Wang Yangming, Mozi and Chinese commentarial editions. Repeated works across areas invite different readings.

targets.A: Adds Chinese intellectual history and commentarial traditions.
targets.N: Supplies philosophical-history and commentary nonfiction candidates.
targets.B: Expands beyond early Chinese sages to later thinkers and annotated traditions.
targets.P: Documents Chinese academic reception of Zhu Xi, Wang Yangming and Mozi.

sources.limits: Study list is not a merit ranking; Chinese edition names do not verify English availability.

sources.title: Libros para que te explote la cabeza
sources.author: Jaime Rubio Hancock
sources.note: A deliberately subjective selection pairs established works with Garces, Camps and Han. It praises philosophical questioning and contextual ethics rather than claiming a universal hierarchy.

targets.N: Supplies critical nonfiction and AI-ethics candidates.
targets.B: Adds Iberian thinkers and distinctions between history and argument.
targets.P: Provides public reception of Garces, Camps, Parfit and Singer.

sources.limits: Some bibliographic/anecdotal details need correction before reuse; English availability for Spanish titles unresolved.

sources.title: 10 Klassiker der Philosophie – in je einem Satz
sources.author: Philomag Redaktion
sources.note: The German selection includes Foot, Weil, Shklar and Murdoch alongside Wittgenstein, Smith and Tocqueville. One-sentence explanations offer reception and candidate evidence only.

targets.A: Adds German editorial reception beyond the usual male-only canon.
targets.N: Identifies ethical and social nonfiction for deeper follow-up.
targets.B: Adds Foot and Murdoch as work candidates.
targets.P: Documents editorial visibility of women moral philosophers.

sources.limits: Thin explanatory depth; selected essays and posthumous compilations need books-only identity review. German dates may be translation dates.
